title: Valid Parenthesis String
statement: A string holds only (, ) and *. Each * may be read as (, as ), or as nothing. Decide whether some choice for the stars makes the whole string balanced: every ( closed by a later ), no ) left over, none left open.

example.caption: Read the * as nothing, or as ). Either way the string balances.

idea.sentence: Track the whole range of how many ( could be open: the fewest (lo) and the most (hi). Stars stretch the range, and the string is valid if 0 is still reachable at the end.

jargon.plain: Every opener has a closer after it, and no closer comes with nothing open.
Every count between lo and hi can be the number of open brackets for some choice of stars.

watch.inputHint: One argument: a string of ( ) and *, e.g. "(*))"

compare.bruteLabel: Try every way to read the stars
compare.unit: readings or characters (rough; brute force is really 3ᵏ for k stars)

rows.name: Brute force
rows.note: Try every choice of ( ) or empty for each of the k stars. Shown as 2ⁿ, the closest shape.

rows.name: Range [lo, hi]
rows.note: One pass. Two integers are all the state.

fast.takeaway: You never pick a reading for any star. The range of open counts covers every reading at once, so one pass decides.

stages.title: Range [0, 0]
stages.note: lo is the fewest open openers possible. hi is the most. Both are 0 before any character.

stages.title: Update the range
stages.note: ( raises both. ) lowers both. * lowers lo and raises hi. If hi drops below 0, even the best reading has too many closers, so return false.

stages.title: Clamp lo at 0
stages.note: A negative count is impossible. Readings that go there are dead, so set lo back to 0.

stages.title: Is 0 possible?
stages.note: After the last character, the string is valid only if lo is 0.

edges.title: Closer first
edges.why: After the first ) the best case is hi = -1. No star could rescue it, so the answer is false right away.

edges.title: Clamp trap
edges.why: Without clamping, the * would drag lo to -1, and the ( would bring it back to 0, wrongly saying yes. Clamped, lo is 1 and the answer is false.

edges.title: Lone star
edges.why: Read it as nothing. lo = -1 is clamped to 0, and 0 is possible.

edges.title: Too many closers
edges.why: The ) after () is already unmatched. Here hi = -1 after the second ), so the later star cannot help.

gotchas.text: Clamp lo at 0 after every character, not only at the end. A negative lo that later climbs back to 0 gives a false yes, as in *(.
Check hi < 0 before clamping lo, and return at once. A dead hi cannot be repaired by later characters.
for _, ch := range s gives runes, so compare with '(' (a rune literal) in the switch. It works because the characters are ASCII.
s[i] is a one-character string, so compare with '(' and not with a char code. A switch on s[i] also works.

recap.key: Keep lo and hi, the fewest and most open brackets over all star readings. Clamp lo at 0, fail if hi < 0, and accept if lo is 0 at the end.
moves: ( raises both, ) lowers both, * lowers lo and raises hi
If lo < 0 set lo = 0. At the end return lo == 0
